September 1, 2026

Army secretary resigns amid clash with Hegseth over Iran war readiness

tags: defence, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Army Secretary Daniel P. Driscoll has resigned from his Pentagon post after months of reported friction with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's office, and Undersecretary Dave Fitzgerald is expected to follow as soon as this week. A source cited by Fox News said Driscoll raised concerns about Army transformation and readiness and that Hegseth blocked those efforts, including by firing the generals responsible for modernization. Driscoll is reported to have taken his concerns directly to President Trump before leaving. The departures come as the war in Iran continues and questions mount over U.S. military readiness.

Massie names alleged Epstein co-conspirators on House floor

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky used a one-minute floor speech to say the government continues to withhold more than 3 million Epstein files a year after the Epstein Files Transparency Act was signed. He announced a second bill intended to move the fight to state courts and force accountability at the Justice Department. Massie then read a list of men and women he described as co-conspirators who should be investigated and prosecuted, including Jes Staley, Leon Black, Les Wexner, David Copperfield, Tom Pritzker, Glenn Dubin, Prince Andrew and Leslie Groff.

Supreme Court lets White House ballroom proceed on standing grounds

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that Trump's $400 million White House ballroom project may continue while a lawsuit proceeds, finding that the National Trust for Historic Preservation likely lacks standing to sue. Standing requires a plaintiff to show a concrete injury the suit would remedy. The reasoning is described as potentially foreclosing other challenges to administration actions, since if the organization charged with historic preservation cannot sue, few private parties could, leaving only the Justice Department in a position to bring a case.

Postal whistleblower says voting order is being implemented despite court block

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A U.S. Postal Service official has filed an emergency whistleblower report, published by the office of Sen. Richard Blumenthal, alleging the Trump administration is defying court orders by pressing ahead with a secretive and rushed implementation of an executive order restricting voting. The report warns of a haphazard rollout that could cause catastrophic failure in the mail ballot system, and says potentially millions of Americans may not receive their mail ballots in time or at all this election cycle. The claims concern the November midterm elections.

U.S. naval blockade halts most Iranian oil exports through Hormuz

tags: politics, markets, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran's oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz have nearly stopped as a tightening U.S. naval blockade increases pressure on Tehran. The blockade is described as achieving what years of sanctions did not.

Iran urges U.S. to honour June interim deal after new strike threats

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran said it would reciprocate if the United States returns to the interim agreement reached in June. The statement follows fresh threats from President Trump of additional strikes, with tensions rising again.

Russian strikes kill 12 near Kyiv on sixth consecutive day

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Russian strikes killed 12 people in and around Kyiv, the sixth straight day of attacks on the Ukrainian capital. Ukraine has warned that its air-defence stocks are running short.

Modi presses Putin to end Ukraine war for humanity's sake

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Vladimir Putin at a meeting in Kyrgyzstan to bring Russia's war in Ukraine to an end, saying the two sides must move in a direction necessary for the good of humanity. Modi said India has consistently raised Ukraine and supports every effort toward peace. He said each day of war pushes humanity backwards while each step toward peace fills it with hope.

Haitian student dies after TPS protection revoked and ankle monitor fitted

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A 20-year-old Haitian immigrant, Pierre de Maas Bell, took his own life after the Trump administration ended Temporary Protected Status for Haitians, according to a Washington Post report. His family said he became increasingly distraught after losing deportation protection, being fitted with an ankle monitor and being summoned to immigration court with a pending asylum claim, and that he felt he was being treated like an animal. He arrived in the United States in 2024 to reunite with family, graduated high school with honours and was a member of JROTC.

EPA approves cancer-linked pesticide for use on food crops

tags: health, climate
sources: @aaronparnas

The Environmental Protection Agency has approved use of the pesticide trifludimoxazin, a persistent chemical described as a known carcinogen, on crops including corn, wheat, oats, soybeans, oranges, apples, peanuts and almonds. The Center for Biological Diversity says the agency approved the chemical while acknowledging potential harms to wildlife and human health, including thyroid tumours in rodent studies, and has sued over the decision. The group says the agency did not assess cancer risk to farm workers who apply the pesticide or to people exposed through contaminated food or water.

Backlash builds over Trump's promotion of AI data centers

tags: tech, politics, climate
sources: @ericmoutsos

President Trump posted in support of communities hosting AI data centers, arguing they bring far lower taxes and widespread job creation, and that many other places want the facilities. Critics responding in the comments, including self-identified supporters, questioned the jobs claim given AI-driven layoffs and said local taxes and power costs have risen sharply where centers have been built. Concerns raised included the strain on farmland and water resources and who ultimately pays for the buildout.

Nepal flood aid dwarfed by ICE equipment contract

tags: climate, immigration, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Six hundred people are dead in flooding in Nepal and 2,500 remain buried under mud. The United States sent $500,000 in relief, after cancelling monitoring programs built for such events in March 2025. In the same week, Immigration and Customs Enforcement signed a no-bid contract worth $16.7 million for gloves that deliver electric shocks.

Lindsay Clancy jury deadlocked after 17 hours of deliberations

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

The jury in the Lindsay Clancy trial told the court it cannot reach a unanimous verdict on charges related to the deaths of her three children after roughly 17 hours of deliberations, describing itself as hopelessly deadlocked. The judge sent the panel back to continue deliberating and retains the option of issuing an Allen charge urging a unanimous decision. If the jury reports deadlock again the court can declare a mistrial, after which prosecutors would decide whether to retry the case. The panel is made up of nine women and three men, and commentary anticipates the outcome being used in arguments over women's participation in juries and the 19th Amendment.

Trump boat parade video renames Lake Ontario amid Canada trade war

tags: politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump and his team circulated a video captioned as showing what "Lake America" would look like, filled with boats flying Trump flags and supporters in MAGA hats. The footage was recorded in South Florida, not on Lake Ontario. The post continues a pattern of taunting Canada during a trade war that is affecting businesses in both countries and raising costs for American families.

Sweden signs $4 billion deal for four French frigates

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Sweden has ordered four frigates from France in a deal worth about $4 billion. The purchase is aimed at strengthening Swedish naval defences and contributing to NATO capability.

U.S. and Indonesia launch Super Garuda Shield exercise

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The United States and Indonesia have begun the Super Garuda Shield military exercise. More than 4,700 personnel are taking part alongside forces from 13 other nations.

Israeli strikes kill four in Gaza after raid to detain Hamas militant

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Four Palestinians were killed in Gaza after an Israeli raid aimed at detaining a Hamas militant triggered strikes. The operation and resulting exchange left the four dead.

Duane Davis found guilty in 1996 killing of Tupac Shakur

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Duane "Keefe D" Davis has been found guilty in connection with the 1996 killing of rapper Tupac Shakur. The verdict closes a case that remained unresolved for nearly three decades.

Hegseth clips resurface after he mocked overweight Canadian cadet instructor

tags: defence, media
sources: @aaronparnas

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth drew attention after mocking a Canadian youth cadet instructor for being overweight. Clips of Hegseth performing physical training with service members, missing a target while throwing an axe on a Fox News segment, and attempting to ride a skateboard have circulated widely in response.

Horizon recalls 53,760 cases of chocolate milk over sealing defect

tags: health
sources: @aaronparnas

Horizon has issued a voluntary recall of 53,760 cases of 1% low-fat chocolate milk sold in 8-ounce cartons in 12- and 18-count boxes. The recall stems from a sealing issue that could cause the milk to spoil before its best-by date, not from a pathogen or contamination, and the company has received no reports of illness or hospitalisation. Affected 12-count boxes carry best-by dates from January 28 to February 3, 2027, and 18-count boxes carry dates of January 31 through February 2, 2027.
